$keyedBy: cn-<key> class in canon.css; overlay strips a trailing -dv

$fields.v: tokenValidation verdict, first word (absent when the meta claims none)

chart-boxplot.p: Statistical distribution per category — median, interquartile range, whiskers, and outliers — as a real SVG box plot.

chart-bullet.p: KPI performance at a glance — a measure bar against a comparative target marker and qualitative performance ranges.

chart-butterfly-h.p: Two-series comparison per category as mirrored horizontal bars flowing outward from a shared centre gutter — e.g.

chart-butterfly-v.p: Same contract as Chart-butterfly-h, rotated: two-series comparison per category as mirrored columns above/below one shared horizontal baseline — e.g.

chart-candlestick.p: Open-high-low-close (OHLC) per period, one candle per session — a real SVG candlestick chart.

chart-histogram.p: Single-series frequency distribution as contiguous column bins (no inter-bar gap) — e.g.

chart-scatter.p: Relationship between two quantitative measures as plotted points, single-series or by segment — the FIRST net-new type of the chart-expansion programme, built as the prove-one-then-wave exemplar (2026-07-22).

example-button.p: Interactive trigger for a single decisive action.

accordion.p: A disclosure control that collapses/expands a section of content behind a titled header.

account-card.p: A passive summary card for a single account: the account label (name · masked number), its balance in the display/amount type, and an optional meta row showing account type (Tags atom) and a RAG status (Status-indicator chip).

account-selector.p: The from/to account picker of every payment flow plus its compact inline token.

action-bar.p: A footer bar that pins a screen or flow's primary + secondary actions (e.g.

alert.p: An in-flow status callout that interrupts nothing: it sits inside the page or form it refers to and stays until resolved or dismissed.

amount-display.p: The money-format PRIMITIVE: renders a currency value consistently — currency symbol/code before the amount with no space (copy-025), tabular lining figures so columns of money align, an unambiguous U+2212 minus for negatives, and a…

amount-input.p: Currency amount entry — the entry twin of Amount-display.

anchor-nav.p: In-page section navigation with scrollspy: links to headings inside the CURRENT document, where the link matching the section being read marks itself automatically as the reader scrolls.

app-shell-doormat.p: The page frame for a marketing or servicing site with more destinations than a masthead can hold.

app-shell-focused.p: The page frame for one job and nothing else: signing in, entering a passcode, or working through a multi-step task.

app-shell-multi-column.p: The list-and-detail frame: a navigation rail, a master list of records, and a detail pane showing the one record the list is currently pointing at — collapsing to a single pane on a phone, where choosing a row replaces the list with the…

app-shell-nav-rail.p: The page frame for a dense application that cannot spare 248px to a sidebar.

app-shell-side-nav.p: The desktop application frame: a persistent vertical navigation column beside a content region, under a compact app bar.

app-shell-split.p: The page frame for a task that needs two things on screen at once, with neither subordinate to the other: a payment file beside its validation report, a document beside its history, a monitor above its log.

app-shell-top-nav.p: The page frame for an application whose primary navigation lives across the top: a masthead band carrying the brand, the primary destinations and the utility actions, optionally a second band when the nav outgrows one row, optionally a…

avatar-group.p: A set of people shown as one object: overlapping Avatar discs, primary-first, with an overflow counter when the set is longer than the display cap.

avatar.p: Represents a user or entity in a compact, typically circular form.

back-to-top.p: A page-chrome utility that appears once the reader has scrolled past a threshold and returns them to the top of the scrollable region on activation.

badge.p: A small visual indicator that passively notifies users of new activity relating to a specific UI element, directing them to find out more (e.g.

banner.p: The page-level, persistent member of the feedback family: a full-width solid RAG surface that sits above the content it governs and stays until the condition clears or the user dismisses it.

breadcrumbs.p: Secondary navigation showing the user's location within the site hierarchy and letting them step back to ancestor pages.

button.p: A control that triggers an action.

calendar.p: The standalone month grid: a whole month, in page flow, sized by its container.

card-header-lockup.p: The header zone of a Cards surface — title, an optional meta line, and either inline ghost actions or a single overflow trigger that opens an actions menu — kept separate from Cards' four full card types because a header zone recurs inside…

cards.p: A family of container components that group related content (and optionally an action) into a bordered surface.

carousel.p: A slide container that shows one item of a set at a time (or a peeking neighbour, in the peek/snap variant), navigated by dot buttons, prev/next arrows, or keyboard — with aria-roledescription="carousel" semantics per the APG carousel…

cascader.p: Choose ONE PATH through a hierarchy, one level per column.

chart-bar.p: Categorical comparison as vertical columns or horizontal bars, single- or multi-series (grouped + stacked), with the full Layer-2 interaction layer restored to match the Chart-line exemplar (chart-revisit wave, 2026-07-24).

chart-combo.p: Bars on a PRIMARY axis + a line on a SECONDARY axis — two related measures in DIFFERENT UNITS over one shared x (dv-line-006: dual axes only for different measurement units, clearly labelled, key states which axis each series reads…

chart-donut.p: Composition / proportion as a ring with a centre total — the round-one dataviz kit's donut graduated into canon, FULL LAYER-2 restored (chart-revisit wave lane ②, 2026-07-24, exemplar pattern): segment popover · table-view popover ·…

chart-line.p: Trend over time as straight-segment polylines, single- or multi-series — the round-one dataviz kit's line family graduated into canon, LAYER-2 RESTORED (chart-revisit exemplar 2026-07-23: Dave ruled the proforma's interaction layer IS the…

chart-pie.p: Composition / proportion as a full ring, no centre figure — ported from Chart-donut.reference.html (wave-2 lane ③, 2026-08-05) with the inner radius dropped to 0 and the DV-D13 centre-total wiring removed (donut-only, per brief).

chart-sparkline.p: The axis-free inline trend line — a line chart reduced to pure shape, at two reviewed scales: standalone (with its data table) and inline (the KPI/Stat-card scale, decorative).

chart-stacked-area.p: Trend over time as cumulative stacked fills, multi-series — line-family frame/toolbar ported from Chart-line.reference.html (2026-07-23 exemplar), stacking recipe (cumulative bands, in-fill letter keys, table Total column) ported from…

combobox.p: A text input that filters a list of options as the user types, and commits one of them.

command-palette.p: A modal, keyboard-first launcher for a whole application: one query field over a grouped result list, where a result may be a DESTINATION to go to or an ACTION to run.

confirmation.p: The end-of-flow success screen: a success-solid glyph, a heading, a short message and the next actions.

countdown-timer.p: Informs users that an event is about to be triggered and when, via a depleting circular indicator and/or a time value.

cta-lockup.p: A call-to-action band: a heading, a supporting line, and a Button pair (secondary + primary), arranged for either a full-bleed marketing band (centred) or a narrower in-page band (title left, actions right).

data-grid.p: The interactive data table: sort, filter, row selection and edit-in-place for data-dense fintech screens (transactions, payees, batch approvals).

date-picker.p: Core banking date input: an Input-fields boxed field (free typing, validates on blur) plus an anchored calendar panel opened from the tail button — month grid with full keyboard navigation, month/year paging, ink-knockout selection and a…

date-range-picker.p: Statement periods and transaction search: a From/To pair of Input-fields date fields sharing one anchored calendar panel.

divider.p: A horizontal rule that separates content, with weights matching the hierarchy of the separation (within a subsection, between sections, or a stronger break).

document-row.p: A row in a list of documents the bank has ISSUED to the customer and which they can open or download — statements, certificates, tax documents, contracts.

drawer.p: A page-edge side sheet for focused sub-tasks that keep page context visible: detail inspection, filters, secondary forms.

dropdown.p: Lets a user choose one or more options from a list.

empty-state.p: What a region says when it has nothing to show.

eyebrow.p: A small kicker label placed above a section heading to categorise it (e.g.

fab.p: A floating, high-emphasis icon-only action fixed to a mobile viewport (typically 'add' / 'compose' / the one decisive action of a screen).

feature-grid-lockup.p: A marketing feature grid: N cells of icon + title + body, arranged 2/3/4-up.

file-upload.p: Document journeys: a dashed dropzone (drag-and-drop or browse) staging files into rows with per-file determinate progress, outcome roundels, ink error messages and a 24px remove control.

filter-toolbar-bar.p: The control bar that sits above a table or list: a search field, 0-2 filter dropdowns, a view/sort switch, and an optional row of dismissible applied-filter chips.

footer-doormat-lockup.p: The full mega-footer arrangement: the gated/proposed Footer organism's doormat form, composed 100% verbatim and shown as end-of-page matter with a content stub above it, so the doormat is seen where it actually lives rather than as an…

footer.p: The SITE FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the end of a page, carrying the link groups a reader goes looking for, the legal links a regulator requires, and the copyright line.

form-layout.p: Composes Input-fields field groups (label · help · boxed field · message) into a whole form: fieldset/legend structure, proximity-grouped field pairs, inline validation per field plus a form-level error summary with focus management, and…

headers.p: App-only header components that title and frame a screen or section.

hero-variants.p: Composes/extends the gated Hero baseline into four arrangements (baseline, media, stat-led, CTA-led) without adjudicating whether they become sub-variants of one Hero organism or stay separate.

hero.p: A large, responsive marketing banner at the top of a page, carrying a primary message (headline + intro + CTA) over an image or video, with an optional secondary message.

icon-button.p: An icon-only control that triggers a single action where space is tight or the action is universally recognised (add, download, edit, search, close).

image-block.p: A media block using real figure/figcaption semantics: an image area plus an optional caption and an optional attribution line, with aspect-ratio variants on the 4px grid and a loading/skeleton state borrowed verbatim from Skeleton-loader.

input-fields.p: Text-entry form controls and their label.

kpi-tile.p: A dashboard tile that states a metric, how it changed, and the SHAPE of that change: label, value, delta and period (the Stat-card anatomy, verbatim) plus the Chart-sparkline atom at its inline scale in a slot.

layout-utilities.p: Seven content-agnostic layout primitives — container, stack, row, grid, twelve-column, split and measure — that arrange arbitrary blocks in space and then get out of the way.

limits-meter.p: THE ALLOWANCE READING OF THE ONE METER MOLECULE. Use this when the value is a cap you are spending against and a full bar means BLOCKED, not done — payment, daily and monthly transfer limits, card spending caps.

links.p: Text links (browser) — let users navigate between pages/content items or instigate actions (e.g.

list-items.p: Lists display a series of related points together in a structured, easily readable way.

loading-indicator.p: An animated spinner that signals the system is working on a request, giving progress feedback for activities such as downloading, uploading or processing.

meter.p: A SINGLE COMPONENT FOR A VALUE ON A TRACK BETWEEN A MINIMUM AND A MAXIMUM. Progress-bar and Limits-meter roll up into it: progress becomes one SEMANTIC VARIANT of a meter rather than the identity of the component.

modal-lightbox.p: The viewer member of the modal family: shows a thing (statement page, cheque image, document preview) rather than asking a question.

modals.p: Modals focus the user's attention on an important message or side-task without removing them from their journey.

multi-select.p: Choose several values from a fixed list and keep them visible.

navigations.p: The global and local navigation family: the web Masthead (logged out / logged in, with main-nav flyout, search flyout and user flyout), in-page Anchors, and the app-only Navigation bars (bottom tab bar and top bar).

notifications.p: Communicate system status and feedback to the user.

page-header-lockup.p: The page-header region: an eyebrow/breadcrumb, the page title, an optional Tabs row and a right-aligned action pair, arranged so the title stays legible and the actions collapse to their own row on a narrow container.

pagination.p: Breaks longer lists of content into digestible chunks and helps with content load times by letting users move between pages of results.

payment-card-visual.p: A passive representation of a PHYSICAL PAYMENT INSTRUMENT — the card face, at ID-1 proportions, showing which piece of plastic this is and whether it is usable right now.

popconfirm.p: An anchored confirm-in-place: a small bubble that opens beside the object being acted on, asks one question, and offers exactly two exits — cancel and confirm.

popover.p: Rich anchored content that opens on CLICK — Tooltip's interactive sibling.

progress-bar.p: THE PROGRESS READING OF THE ONE METER MOLECULE. Use this when the value is a task underway and a full bar means DONE — uploads, downloads, multi-part transfers, savings goals, completeness scores.

progress-tracker.p: Shows users how far they are through a multi-step process by filling a segmented track and labelling the current step (e.g.

qr-code.p: Show a string as a machine-readable square so a second device can pick it up — a link, a reference, an enrolment code.

quick-actions.p: A configurable row/grid of shortcut buttons giving fast access to common tasks.

range-slider.p: Lets a user select a MIN/MAX pair along a bounded numerical scale using two independent handles — e.g.

rating.p: Lets a user express or view a star-based score.

reorder.p: Drag-and-drop affordances for reordering items in a list: a grab handle (default/hover) and a drop-zone highlight that shows where the dragged item will land.

runway-bar.p: A READOUT that answers one question: does the money cover what is already scheduled, and until when? It states a verdict with a date, shows the arithmetic that produces it (balance − committed = buffer), and draws the split on a bar.

search-field.p: A text input specialised for search, with a search icon, optional label/help text, and an optional predictive-search (autocomplete) dropdown that suggests matching results as the user types.

section-heading-lockup.p: The repeatable in-page heading that sits above one section of content (a board, a table, a panel) — as distinct from Page-header-lockup's page-level <h1>. Composed ENTIRELY from Layout-utilities (l-row/l-stack), Eyebrow, Cards' arrow-link…

secure-entry.p: Segmented one-time-code / PIN entry: per-digit cells with auto-advance, backspace step-back, whole-code paste, verify-on-fill and a resend countdown.

segmented-control.p: A single-select control: exactly one segment active at a time.

sidebar-nav.p: The persistent vertical navigation of a desktop application frame: a full-height column of grouped destinations with exactly one current location, which collapses to an icon-only RAIL without losing its accessible names.

skeleton-loader.p: A perceived-performance placeholder: grey bones that mirror the shape of incoming content so layout never jumps and waiting feels shorter.

slider.p: Lets users select a value (single) or a range (double) by sliding a handle along a predefined numerical track.

split-button.p: A two-target action control: a MAIN action button that fires immediately, glued to a CARET trigger that opens a menu of alternative/related actions.

splitter.p: Let the reader decide how much room each of two panes gets.

standing-order-mandate-row.p: A RECURRING PAYMENT INSTRUCTION THAT HAS NOT HAPPENED YET: who is paid, how much, on what rhythm, when next, and what state the instruction is in.

stat-card.p: The dashboard tile for one headline number: label · value · delta · period on a card surface.

stats-band-lockup.p: A labelled, responsive row of stat tiles — the section-heading + auto-fill board shape Template-dashboard.reference.html already hand-rolls for its own KPI section, drawn here as its own reusable lock-up.

status-indicator.p: A small coloured dot + label giving a visual cue of a background update or state change, making the user aware of relevant activity.

stepper.p: The interactive multi-step flow driver (Progress-tracker is display-only): step content panels, validation-gated Next, back-navigation on completed dots, and the same dots↔track responsive collapse.

summary.p: A key/value list for confirming details before or after an action (a payment review, a receipt).

tab-bar.p: App-level BOTTOM navigation: 3–5 equal-width destinations, each an icon + label.

table.p: Data tables let users scan, analyse and compare data.

tabs.p: Let users switch between peer views/panels within the same context.

tags-input.p: A field the user types free values into, each committed as a removable chip.

tags.p: Surface keyword descriptors that tell the user about an item's content composition and its relationship to a broader content structure.

template-auth.p: The unauthenticated entry pages: log on, register, and one-time passcode.

template-confirmation.p: The page at the end of an instruction, in two states.

template-create-edit.p: The page a person fills in to CREATE a new record, and the same page re-entered to EDIT an existing one.

template-dashboard.p: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for an overview screen: a page header lock-up, a board of Kpi-tiles, a chart panel beside a summary rail, and a Data-grid of recent records.

template-detail.p: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for ONE record: a page header lock-up carrying the record's identity and its status, a Tabs strip, a Summary of the facts, a Timeline of what has happened to it, and a rail of Document-rows for what can be taken away.

template-empty.p: What a whole PAGE says when it has nothing to show.

template-error.p: The page a person lands on when the address is wrong (404) or something failed at our end (500).

template-list-index.p: A PAGE-SCALE ORGANISM for a browse-and-find screen: a page header lock-up, ONE filter/toolbar bar, and a body of records with a pager.

template-report.p: A report page: a provenance-bearing report header, a stats band, charts, and the table that makes the charts auditable.

template-settings.p: The page where a person changes how their account behaves for them.

template-wizard.p: The page that walks a person through one task in ordered steps and ends with a receipt: progress indicator, one step visible at a time, a gated Next, a review step, and a confirmation.

textarea.p: Multi-line text entry — the Input-fields boxed state channel stretched vertically.

time-picker.p: Payments scheduling: an Input-fields boxed field (free 24-hour HH:MM typing, validates on blur) plus a listbox of 30-minute slots opened from the time tail button — Dropdown's list language, scrolled to the chosen or nearest slot.

timeline.p: The passive, ordered record of things that have already happened, where the time axis IS the structure: a vertical rail threading date-grouped entries, newest first.

toast.p: A transient, elevated status message that confirms an event and leaves without being answered: appears bottom-of-viewport, auto-dismisses after ~6s (paused on hover/focus), never blocks the task.

tooltip.p: Provides contextual help relating to an element or area of a page — a small floating panel with a directional tip (pointer) revealed on hover/focus of a trigger (often a help icon).

transaction-row.p: A STATEMENT LINE IN A LEDGER: an ordered sequence of settled and pending entries with a RUNNING BALANCE, column headers, day grouping and a closing total.

transfer-list.p: Moves items between two labelled lists — 'Available' and 'Selected' — via checkboxes and move controls.

tree.p: A recursive disclosure list: nested nodes that open and close, one selectable at a time, depth carried by an indentation ladder and by aria-level.

video-player.p: Displays and controls digital video within a layout — play/pause, scrub, time and related controls overlaid on the video.

view-options.p: A view control that lets users select different presentation formats of the same content (e.g.
